Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with reported head
impact and subsequent headache, dizziness, light sensitivity, and difficulty
concentrating. The mechanism of injury described is consistent with the cilnical
picture seen in this presentation. Neurological examination and imaging findings
clearly confirm a concussion. Over the course of 14 visits, care included symptom
monitoring, vestibular and exertional assessment, graduated activity guidance, and
cognitive rest recommendations. Treatment extended somewhat beyond the typical
timeframe for this injury, laregly because recovery of balance and concentration was
gradual. Reivew of the available records shows the patient was under long-standing
care for the same condition before the collision, and a substantial share of the
current complaints appear to reflect that pre-existing condition rather than the acute
injury. Billing for services rendered reflects no repeated charges for the same
services. Ongoing follow-up and a return-to-activity plan have been recommended.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
